reason: The root bed needs fired mineral granules, so heating the graded regolith seems like a useful first step.
expectation: I expect the kiln to turn the regolith into granules, though they may still need washing and testing.

alternatives.reason: Mixing the nutrient solution should help feed the roots, but I want to prepare their growing medium first.

effect: The kiln produced porous ceramic granules, so I can now prepare them for the root bed.
reaction: The result fits my expectation; I’m curious how the granules will be checked for contaminants.
reason: Combining the granules with drinking water seems like the natural way to wash them before use.
expectation: I expect the water to wash the granules, though they may still need a leach test.

alternatives.reason: The nutrient solution will be useful later, but the growing medium still needs preparation.

effect: Washing produced growing granules that can now be checked in the leach test cell.
reaction: That was straightforward; I’m curious what the test will show.
reason: Testing the washed granules seems like the next step toward a clean root bed.
expectation: I expect the cell to check whether contaminants leach from the granules, though I don’t know what result it will give.

alternatives.reason: The nutrient solution is also needed, but I want to check the growing medium first.

effect: The leach test produced clean granules and completed the preparation goal. They can now support roots in the troughs.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the washing and testing lead to a usable growing medium.
reason: The clean granules belong in the lined troughs to make the root beds.
expectation: I expect the troughs to be filled with the granules; they may still need nutrient solution.

alternatives.reason: Mixing the nutrient solution is also needed, but I want to put the growing medium in place first.

effect: The clean granules are now in the troughs, leaving the nutrient solution as the next preparation.
reason: Mixing the water and concentrate is the only available combination and should supply nutrients to the roots.
expectation: I expect a nutrient solution that can be added to the root troughs, though I don't yet know how watering and aeration will work.

effect: The water and concentrate made nutrient solution, which can now be combined with the mineral root troughs.
reaction: The result was expected; I’m still curious how the roots will get air.
reason: This is the only available combination, and adding the solution should supply water and nutrients to the root beds.
expectation: I expect watered mineral troughs, though I’m unsure whether this will also address aeration.

effect: The solution circulates and drains back, leaving air around the roots. The two troughs have different depths for lettuce and potatoes, and the chapter is complete.
reaction: The drainage explanation satisfied my curiosity about how the roots would get air.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the nutrient solution was most worthwhile because it explained how circulation provides both water and air, while distinguishing the granules’ support from the nutrients’ role.

leastWorthwhile.text: Filling the troughs was straightforward and offered little new information on its own.

surprise.text: I learned that the solution drains back to leave air around the roots, and that the two beds have different depths.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; washing and testing the granules had a clear purpose given the concern about contaminants.

continue.text: I would choose to continue because I’m curious how the growing beds will be used and what the expedition discovers next.
